extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and clinicians invited to peer-review manuscripts for The Lancet journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for external peer reviewers on how to evaluate manuscripts submitted to The Lancet journals, including scope of critique, ethical expectations, reviewer selection, and recommendation categories. Focuses on what reviewers should report and which additional expert reviews are sought for research articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a written evaluation of the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are asked to provide a written evaluation of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should produce a written critique that assesses the manuscript's content and quality; this is the primary deliverable editors use to judge the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask questions and request clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should ask questions of the authors or request clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unclear points, request additional information or explanations from authors where necessary to judge validity, reproducibility, or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise editors on acceptability (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should advise editors on whether, based on what is presented to them, it is acceptable for publication, could be acceptable after revision, or should be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear recommendation tied to the review (Accept / Acceptable after revision / Reject) and justify the recommendation with reference to the manuscript's strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical evaluation should add clarity to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help improve the presentation, organization, and clear communication of methods, results, and interpretation so readers can understand the work's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and report uncertainties and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should acknowledge and report both uncertainties and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out limitations in design, analysis, and interpretation, and identify where conclusions are uncertain or unsupported by the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place new work in the context of the totality of available evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique should place new work in the context of the totality of available evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the manuscript relates to existing literature and whether the authors accurately and adequately situate their findings within the broader evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent over-interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should help prevent over-interpretation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag claims that exceed the data, recommend tempering conclusions, and suggest framing that accurately reflects the study's scope and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare financial and non-financial conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to declare any financial and non-financial academic or intellectual conflicts that might have the potential to influence their critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relationships, funding, intellectual positions, or other interests that could bias your review; follow journal procedures for conflict disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise: relevant scientific or clinical expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors identify and invite independent experts with relevant scientific or clinical expertise to review the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should possess topic-specific knowledge sufficient to evaluate the study's design, methods, analyses, and clinical or scientific implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary knowledge and skills among reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors ensure reviewers' complementary knowledge and skills provide a thorough review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team deliberately selects reviewers whose combined expertise covers clinical, methodological, statistical, and disciplinary perspectives to produce an in-depth critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of reviewer perspectives (different expertise and locations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors send manuscripts to reviewers with different expertise and from different locations, deliberately seeking reviews that provide an in-depth critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diverse geographic and specialty perspectives are used to reduce bias, broaden assessment, and enhance generalizability of the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical review for all research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: All research articles are also sent to a statistical reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical reviewers assess study design, statistical methods, analyses, and reporting of results; their input is required for quantitative research submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include other expert reviewers when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, other experts such as modellers, data scientists, health economists, and patients with lived experience are invited to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite domain-specific experts (e.g., modelling, data science, economic evaluation) and stakeholder perspectives (e.g., patient representatives) to evaluate specialized methods or the relevance/impact of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to ICMJE and COPE ethical guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lancet journals follow ICMJE Recommendations and COPE guidelines on ethical peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should conduct reviews in accordance with ICMJE and COPE principles for conduct, reporting, editing, publication ethics, and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision categories
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, editors make decisions: Accept; Acceptable after revision; Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' recommendations inform but do not solely determine editorial decisions; provide clear reasons and actionable suggestions linked to one of these categories.
